assessment: A strong conceptual round with clear, well-organised answers. Depth dropped on fine-tuning trade-offs, and the bracket-matching solution missed the empty-stack case.
strengths: Explained overfitting with a concrete train-versus-validation example
Talked through the running_sum approach before writing any code
improvements: Compare fine-tuning against prompting or retrieval when the question invites it
Test the edge cases out loud, such as a closing bracket with nothing to match

questions.question: What is overfitting, and how would you detect it?
questions.comment: Accurate and well structured; naming regularisation as the fix would have rounded it off.

questions.question: What is the difference between pretraining and fine-tuning a language model?
questions.comment: Got the distinction right but stayed at the surface; mention data scale and catastrophic forgetting.

questions.question: Implement running_sum: given a list of integers, return a new list where element i is the sum of the first i plus one input elements.
questions.comment: Clean single pass with a running total; a clear name for the accumulator would help.

questions.question: Implement is_balanced: given a string containing only round, square, and curly brackets, return True if every bracket is closed by the matching bracket in the correct order.
questions.comment: Right idea with a stack, but popping from an empty stack fails on input that starts with a closing bracket.
